name: Michael, Sword of the Highest Gate
loreTies: Michael embodies radiant guardianship, holy war, sword judgment, and threshold defense within The Radiant Hierarchies.
The Choir-Vault Gate allows this deity to enter Ascension-era dungeon routes without collapsing the individuality of other Realms.
Empyrean culture, symbols, weapons, and divine law shape every ability, artifact, silhouette, and combat choice.
shortBackstory: Michael, Sword of the Highest Gate, is a playable god in Mythos Gates: Ascension. Michael is the true source-realm divinity behind the mythology — radiant guardianship, holy war, sword judgment, and threshold defense. Ascension expands divine power during the current Gate crisis; it does not turn a mortal into a god.

chapters.title: Divine Origin
chapters.text: Michael is not a mortal hero inspired by myth. Michael is the actual god recognized by Empyrean source culture, born from the supernatural laws of The Radiant Hierarchies. Their domain — radiant guardianship, holy war, sword judgment, and threshold defense — determines their symbols, weapons, posture, combat instincts, and relationship to sacred authority.

chapters.title: Faction Bond
chapters.text: Within Empyrean, Michael expresses the civilization rather than merely representing it. Their visual identity must carry the materials, beauty standards, divine symbols, and sacred rules of The Radiant Hierarchies. Their gameplay role, Defender, must grow from mythology first and mechanics second.

chapters.title: Mythos Gate Wound
chapters.text: During the Ascension era, Michael can interact with The Choir-Vault Gate because divine beings are intrinsically connected to their Realms. The Gate does not become a simple teleportation portal; it is a mysterious boundary where separate mythological realities become traversable. Michael understands some rites of crossing, but not the complete origin of the Mythos Gates.

chapters.title: Dungeon Role
chapters.text: When selected by the player, Michael enters the dungeon alone as one god or goddess against multiple enemies. No army follows. No squad shares control. Every room, trap, shrine, relic, elite, and boss encounter must test how radiant guardianship, holy war, sword judgment, and threshold defense survives pressure from creatures, rival Realm laws, and unstable Gate conditions.

chapters.title: Ascension Conflict
chapters.text: Ascension is the current story arc, not the permanent end-state of the Mythos Gates universe. For Michael, Ascension means restoration, awakening, evolution, or expansion of existing divine power. Their personal conflict is to recover strength without reducing Empyrean mythology into raw fuel for the crisis.

relationshipHooks: Faction witnesses interpret how Michael crosses The Choir-Vault Gate.
Rival deities challenge the limits of cross-Realm travel.
Dungeon lore pickups reveal Gate mystery without resolving the full origin.
developmentStatus: Playable deity backstory aligned to Mythos Gates identity, one-deity dungeon runs, current Ascension arc, and preserved Lore Codex canon.
mythicSource: source culture humans later copied as angelic and heavenly lore
visualCanon: Oriel is an edict-keeper formed by angelic hierarchy and living record law. Their glass tablets, bell-metal seals, layered halos, quiet dread, and wing geometry should feel like the origin of later angel-scribe legends.
title: Sword of the Highest Gate

mythosGatesCanon.identityRule: Michael is the actual god of Empyrean source mythology, never a mortal hero or generic champion.
mythosGatesCanon.arcRule: Ascension restores, awakens, evolves, or expands existing divine power; it does not make the character a god for the first time.
mythosGatesCanon.mysteryRule: The backstory may reveal how this deity interacts with the Mythos Gates, but must not resolve the full origin of the Gates.
